title: The skull of a saint that was discovered during renovations

input.lead: Ambrose Barlow was found guilty of treason and sentenced to death in 1641
input.summary: Ambrose Barlow was found guilty of treason and sentenced to death in 1641
input.evidence_text: The skull of a saint that was discovered during renovations - BBC News Image caption, The skull of St Ambrose Barlow is on display at Wardley Hall By Jen Dale North West Published 42 minutes ago On 25 April 1641, Ambrose Barlow celebrated a secret Easter Sunday mass at Morleys Hall near Astley in Greater Manchester. But, by the end of the service, the building had been surrounded by a 400-strong armed group led by a local vicar. "King Charles I issued a decree stating that all Catholic priests must leave within a month...and if they didn't, they would face the consequences of treason," said the Right Reverend John Arnold, the Bishop of Salford. King Charles I wanted to prove that he supported the Protestant faith while keeping his political enemies at bay as parliament were suspicious of his Catholic wife. The congregation urged Ambrose Barlow to hide but Arnold said he refused and instead ordered the doors to be opened and surrendered peacefully. "He didn't make any attempt to avoid arrest," said Arnold. "He was really concerned for the safety of the people attending mass - about 150 of them." Image source, Diocese of Salford Image caption, The Right Reverend John Arnold said records showed Ambrose Barlow had a "good sense of humour" and was "very mild in his character" He was taken to Lancaster Castle where he was imprisoned. After four months, he was put on trial, charged with being a priest. He was found guilty of treason and sentenced to death. "On 10 September, which is now his feast day, he was hung, drawn, and quartered," said Arnold. "And his skull was put on a pike as a demonstration to people that this is what happens if you are a Catholic." It was a warning to all who refused to conform to the state religion. It opened for traffic from January 1, 1894. It cost more than £15m, equivalent today to £2.1bn Queen Victoria officially opened the canal on May 21, 1894 An estimated 17,000 workers grafted to make the 36 miles waterway from Salford to the Irish Sea. title: Manchester study reveals pupils most at risk of school suspension - and what may help them | About Manchester

input.lead: New Manchester research suggests tackling the factors behind suspensions could help prevent repeated exclusions and support vulnerable pupils School suspensions are associated with a complex combination of socioeconomic disadvantage, special educational needs, peer relationships
input.summary: New Manchester research suggests tackling the factors behind suspensions could help prevent repeated exclusions and support vulnerable pupils School suspensions are associated with a complex combination of socioeconomic disadvantage, special educational needs, peer relationships
input.evidence_text: New Manchester research suggests tackling the factors behind suspensions could help prevent repeated exclusions and support vulnerable pupils School suspensions are associated with a complex combination of socioeconomic disadvantage, special educational needs, peer relationships and pupils’ experiences of school, according to new research from The University of Manchester The study analysed survey responses from more than 19,000 secondary school pupils linked to administrative records across Hampshire & Isle of Wight, to examine a wide range of factors associated with whether pupils were suspended and how often suspensions occurred Researchers found pupils receiving special educational needs (SEN) support or with an Education, Health and Care Plan (EHCP) were more than twice as likely to be suspended than pupils without SEN, while those eligible for free school meals were also at increased risk The analysis also identified a number of factors associated with lower suspension risk, including pupils feeling that they belonged at school, being satisfied with their academic attainment, having positive relationships with school staff and having stronger emotion regulation sk By contrast, higher levels of peer pressure, experiences of bullying, and recent substance use were associated with an increased likelihood of suspension

Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. Listen Unafraid to push the boundaries of eroticism and performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic asks its audience a timeless question: What are our bodies truly for?
